Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize a faculty development workshop titled “Mastering Orthoptics: From Clinical Assessment to Diagnosis and Management.” Mr. Imran Khalid Bhutta (PhD Medical Education Scholar, M.Phil Orthoptics, King Edward Medical University) will be invited as the facilitator. The workshop will provide faculty members with advanced knowledge and hands-on training in the clinical assessment, diagnosis, and management of squint patients. The activity will be organized by Dr. Sidra Sattar and Ms. Komal Mushtaq, under the supervision of Ms. Tahira Kalsoom, Head, Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences.
Expected Outcome: The activity will enhance faculty members’ clinical knowledge and practical skills in orthoptics and squint management, promote faculty development, and strengthen professional and institutional linkages.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize a faculty industrial visit to E. Plomer & Co. The visit will particularly focus on contact lenses, with special emphasis on Rigid Gas Permeable (RGP) lens fitting, lens patterns, manufacturing processes, and practical aspects of contact lens production and fitting. The visit will provide faculty members with an opportunity to gain industry-based knowledge and practical exposure.
Expected Outcome: The visit will enhance faculty members’ understanding of RGP contact lenses, fitting techniques, lens patterns, and industry practices. It will also strengthen academic–industry linkage and provide opportunities for future professional collaboration.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize an eye screening camp for the transgender community during the second week of October 2026. The activity will provide basic eye examinations, vision screening, identification of ocular conditions, and appropriate referral and guidance to the participants. The activity will be organized by Dr. Sidra Sattar and Ms. Komal Mushtaq, under the supervision of Ms. Tahira Kalsoom, Head, Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences.
Expected Outcome: The activity will provide accessible eye care services to an underserved community, facilitate early identification of vision and ocular problems, and strengthen the department’s community engagement and social responsibility initiatives.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize an eye screening camp at the Central Jail during the second week of October 2026. The camp will provide basic eye examinations, visual acuity assessment, screening for common ocular conditions, and appropriate referral and guidance for individuals requiring further eye care. The activity will be organized by Dr. Sidra Sattar and Ms. Komal Mushtaq, under the supervision of Ms. Tahira Kalsoom, Head, Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences.
Expected Outcome: The activity will provide essential eye screening services to an underserved population, promote early detection of ocular and visual problems, and strengthen community outreach and institutional linkages.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize a World Sight Day celebration at The University of Lahore on 15 October 2026. The event will include an optometry-related quiz for students, with participation from students of other universities to promote inter-university engagement and academic collaboration. Reports of the eye screening camps and community outreach activities conducted by the department will also be presented during the event. The activity will be organized by Dr. Sidra Sattar and Ms. Komal Mushtaq, under the supervision of Ms. Tahira Kalsoom, Head, Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences.
Target Partner / Institution: Students and Optometry Departments of other universities
Expected Outcome: The event will promote awareness regarding eye health and vision care, encourage academic interaction among students from different institutions, enhance students’ knowledge through healthy academic competition, and highlight the department’s community eye-care and outreach initiatives.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize a hands-on training workshop on Rigid Gas Permeable (RGP) Contact Lenses in November 2026. The workshop will focus on practical techniques for RGP lens selection, fitting, assessment, and management, with particular emphasis on contact lens fitting for patients with keratoconus. The activity will be organized by Dr. Sidra Sattar and Ms. Komal Mushtaq, under the supervision of Ms. Tahira Kalsoom, Head, Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences. An expert facilitator from the relevant field will be invited to provide specialized training and practical demonstrations
Expected Outcome: The workshop will enhance faculty members’ practical skills in RGP contact lens fitting and equip participants with advanced techniques for the assessment and management of keratoconus patients through specialized contact lens interventions.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will organize a guest lecture in the form of a webinar on Optometry Awareness in December 2026. An expert speaker from the field of optometry will be invited to discuss the scope, role, and importance of optometry in eye and vision care. The webinar will provide students and faculty members with an opportunity to enhance their understanding of the profession and engage with an experienced professional from the field.
Expected Outcome: The webinar will enhance awareness regarding the role and scope of optometry, provide students with exposure to professional perspectives, and strengthen academic and professional linkages with experts in the field.

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will conduct weekly mentoring activities throughout the semester to support students’ academic, personal, and professional development. Each faculty member will be assigned three to four student groups, with 15 students in each group. Each group will have one mentoring session per month. The sessions will provide an open and supportive environment where students can share their concerns, discuss challenges they may be facing, and seek appropriate guidance and support from their assigned faculty mentor.
Target Partner / Institution: Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences / Enrolled Students
Expected Outcome: The mentoring sessions will provide students with a safe and supportive platform to voice their concerns, promote student wellbeing, strengthen faculty–student relationships, and facilitate timely guidance and support for students facing personal or other challenges.
How Many (original): 03–04 Student Groups per Faculty Member, 15 Students per Group / 01 Session per Group per Month

Brief Description: The Department of Optometry and Vision Sciences, Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, will conduct curriculum feedback meetings with the CRs and GRs of each class throughout the semester.
